newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Snowstorms trap at least 1,200 people in Andes.
newsitem.headline: Snowstorms trap at least 1,200 people in Andes.

text.p: Severe snowstorms have stranded more than 1,200 people on the Chile-Argentine border high in the Andes mountains, weather authorities reported on Monday.
The blizzard affecting Argentina's northeastern Mendoza province is unlikely to ebb until Thursday and is blamed on the El Nino wind factor coming from the Pacific Ocean.
"El Nino usually starts in the southern hemisphere during the summer, but this year it's happening in the winter," a National Weather Bureau official in Buenos Aires said.
On Sunday, Border and Civil Guard troops rescued 13 miners trapped on the Andes in La Rioja province, but 36 others remain grounded in the mining town of Pena Negra.
However, all of those trapped received foodstuffs and are out of danger, the authorities said.

On the Chilean side, where roads were blocked by 18 feet (six metres) of snow, the 200 travelers were holed up in a customs office and nearby buildings at Los Libertadores pass with adequate food and heating but no word on when they might be able to leave.
Air force rescuers brought about 30 people, mostly women and children, out by helicopter on Sunday but abandoned operations when snowstorms resumed.
